content.text: Most tutorials about building a [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-stores-kyc-payments-first-principles-definitive-2|COREMERCH guide to digital]] store focus on the storefront. The storefront is the last thing you should configure. The backend is what makes the store work — and the backend is what most creators get wrong when they try to build without a clear sequence. In Stack 01, Google Apps Script serves as the backend Web App — it receives the NOWPayments webhook, validates the signature, confirms the transaction on-chain, logs the order to Google Sheets, and sends the delivery email via Gmail. In Stack 02, Cloudflare Workers replaces Apps Script with a faster, more scalable serverless backend that integrates natively with [[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-what-5|GitHub Pages]].io/store/blog/how-supabase-order-database-digital-stores-complete-infrastructure-3|supabase]] for order storage and Resend for email delivery. Configure the backend first, set the webhook endpoint URL in NOWPayments second, build the storefront third, and test on mainnet fourth.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

COREMERCH's Sovereign Commerce infrastructure is designed to address the shortcomings of Stripe and other payment processors. By leveraging Cloudflare Pages and Cloudflare Workers, you can deploy a scalable and secure digital store that accepts crypto payments. This infrastructure is not a workaround, but a base-layer solution that empowers you to own your commerce stack. With Cloudflare Pages, you can host your digital products with ease, and Cloudflare Workers enable you to write custom backend logic to integrate with NOWPayments, a payment processor that supports over 300 cryptocurrencies. By decoupling payment processing from the platform, you regain control over your commerce infrastructure and can escape the limitations of traditional payment processors.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, you'll need to gather a few essential components. First, you'll need to create a Cloudflare account and set up a new project. Next, you'll need to choose a payment processor, such as NOWPayments, and integrate it with Cloudflare Workers. You'll also need to configure your domain and SSL certificate to ensure a secure connection. Finally, you'll need to design and implement your digital product store, including creating product listings, setting up payment options, and configuring order fulfillment. While this may seem daunting, COREMERCH's Sovereign Blueprint provides a step-by-step guide to help you deploy your crypto store in as little as 4-6 hours.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

One of the key advantages of COREMERCH's infrastructure is the ability to configure a payment and delivery pipeline that's tailored to your specific needs. With Cloudflare Workers, you can write custom logic to integrate with NOWPayments and automate payment processing. You can also configure delivery options to ensure that customers receive their digital products promptly and securely. By decoupling payment processing from the platform, you can escape the limitations of traditional payment processors and create a more seamless customer experience.

You'll need to test your payment processing and delivery pipeline to ensure that everything is working correctly. Once you're confident that your infrastructure is secure and functioning properly, you can go live and start processing transactions. With NOWPayments, you can accept over 300 cryptocurrencies and enjoy a 0.5% fee on all transactions.

As your digital product store grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to ensure that it can handle increased traffic and transactions. With COREMERCH's Sovereign Commerce infrastructure, you can easily scale your payment and delivery pipeline to meet the demands of your growing business.
